rounds.hypothesis: Per diagnose.json: no wait4 code is wrong. The single wrong value is the PID_MAX ceiling itself. PID_MAX = u32::MAX / 2 = i32::MAX is advertised verbatim through /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max, so the test's pid_max + 1 = 2147483648 does not fit in the signed pid_t that wait4 takes and arrives as the bit pattern 0x80000000. sys_wait4 casts it to i32::MIN, and ProcessFilter::from_id's first arm correctly returns ESRCH for that one unnegatable input. Restoring the headroom Linux keeps above its ceiling should make pid_max + 1 an ordinary positive pid_t again and let the request fall through to the generic ECHILD path.
rounds.change: Changed PID_MAX at kernel/src/process/posix_thread/mod.rs:425 from `u32::MAX / 2` to `4 * 1024 * 1024` (4194304), Linux's 64-bit PID_MAX_LIMIT. Replaced the 'chosen arbitrarily' FIXME with a doc comment recording the value's provenance in include/linux/threads.h and, more importantly, why the headroom above the ceiling is load-bearing rather than incidental, so the constant is not raised back to the sign boundary later. Narrowed the surviving FIXME to the part that is still true: the value is not yet writable through the sysctl. Touched neither process_filter.rs nor wait4.rs. Uncommented wait402 in test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt:1819.
rounds.outcome: green on the first round: 'Passed: 1, Failed: 0, Broken: 0, Skipped: 0, Warnings: 0' and 'All conformance tests passed.' The 0 broken count also confirms setup()'s read of /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max still succeeded against the new value.

layer: kernel/src/process/posix_thread/mod.rs, the PID allocation policy layer that owns the PID_MAX ceiling. This matches diagnose.json's owning_layer. It owns the invariant because it is the single definition of the ceiling that both the allocator (allocate_posix_tid) and the procfs sysctl re-export, so correcting it here fixes the reporting path and every other consumer at once. Deliberately not patched at the syscall layer: the host probe in diagnose.json shows real Linux returns ESRCH for wait4(INT_MIN), so relaxing ProcessFilter::from_id's i32::MIN arm to ECHILD would have turned this test green by trading away a genuinely correct behavior. Verified in-tree that from_id's arms are still arm-for-arm Linux's kernel_wait4, including that ESRCH guard.
generalizes: The fix is a value correction to a shared constant with no branch on anything the test supplies, so it cannot be overfitted to wait402's inputs. It corrects behavior for inputs the test never supplies and callers it never walks. (1) ProcessFilter::from_id is shared by sys_wait4 and sys_kill per its own comment, so kill(pid_max + 1, sig) misreported ESRCH on identical arithmetic and is fixed by the same change; the test only exercises wait4. (2) /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max stopped handing i32::MAX to every userspace program that sizes PID arithmetic or allocates a PID-indexed table from it, which is the ps-and-monitoring-tools case and is far larger than this test. (3) The cgroupfs pids.max bound at cgroupfs/controller/pids.rs:114 validates writes against PID_MAX and merely tightens, from accepting absurd limits up to i32::MAX to a sane ceiling; 'max' still maps to u32::MAX independently, so that path keeps working. No caller regresses from the lower ceiling: grepped every PID_MAX and pid_max reference in kernel/ and ostd/ and those three are the complete set, and allocate_posix_tid only warns when it crosses the ceiling and still returns the tid, so allocation behavior is unchanged at any reachable thread count. Confirmed no code or test hardcodes the old value: the only 2147483647 and u32::MAX / 2 hits in-tree are an unrelated fixed-point type and a procfs fd number.
fix_summary: Lowers the advertised PID ceiling from i32::MAX to Linux's 64-bit PID_MAX_LIMIT of 4194304, restoring the headroom the invariant requires so that pid_max + 1 remains a representable positive pid_t. wait4(4194305) now takes from_id's final else arm and builds ProcessFilter::WithPid(4194305); wait.rs finds no matching child or tracee and returns ECHILD, instead of overflowing into the i32::MIN process-group guard and reporting ESRCH. Designed against Asterinas's own abstraction rather than transplanting Linux's: Asterinas expresses the ceiling as a single compile-time `pub const PID_MAX: u32` consulted by allocate_posix_tid and re-exported to the procfs sysctl, which already lines up structurally with Linux's compile-time limit plus sysctl, so only the value diverged and no restructuring was warranted. Notably Asterinas keeps this as a constant where Linux scales a runtime pid_max by CPU count in pid_idr_init; the constant is the existing abstraction and making it a runtime tunable is the separate, still-open FIXME about supporting writes to the sysctl, so this fix stays inside the constant. Chose PID_MAX_LIMIT (4194304) over PID_MAX_DEFAULT (32768) because it is the value the host baseline actually advertises, which keeps the guest's reported ceiling consistent with the reference kernel the suite is judged against, and because a higher ceiling is the safer change for an allocator that cannot yet recycle PIDs.
